cards.b: Directly involves the main pancreatic duct → dilatation + mucin production. Very high malignant risk (~80%). Risk rises with duct diameter. Normal duct ≈2–3 mm; duct ≈10 mm = very high risk. May present with pain, weight loss, ± jaundice. Diagnosis: CT, MRI/MRCP, EUS. Aspirate shows mucin, high amylase, high CEA. Treatment: surgical resection.

Arises from a side branch rather than the main duct. Malignant potential correlates with cyst size and high- risk imaging features: mural nodule, enhancing solid component, progressive increase in size. Small lesions are commonly incidental.
Both main-duct and side-branch involvement may occur — treat with the higher-risk (main-duct) approach.
